output.question: Has Oracle announced layoffs?
output.answer: Oracle has cut jobs in several rounds in 2026, but it has not made a formal public announcement with a total; the numbers come from state WARN filings, its annual filing and press reports. The latest round reportedly began on September 14, 2026. WARN filings dated that day show about 800 employees in Washington (Seattle, 359) and California (Redwood City, Santa Clara and Pleasanton, 441) losing their jobs on November 13, 2026, and Oracle said these layoffs are expected to be permanent. That came after a late-March round of about 1,778 U.S. cuts, which brings WARN-documented U.S. cuts in 2026 to at least 2,578. Global headcount fell from about 162,000 to about 141,000 in the fiscal year ending May 31, 2026, though that drop also includes attrition and is not a layoff count.

key_facts.fact: WARN filings dated Sept. 14, 2026 show about 800 Oracle employees in Washington (359) and California (441: 279 Redwood City, 99 Santa Clara, 63 Pleasanton) set to lose their jobs on Nov. 13, 2026.
Oracle said the layoffs are expected to be permanent and that the Seattle locations are not closing. The article attributes no other comment to Oracle.
A late-March 2026 round produced 1,778 WARN-listed U.S. job losses (WA 475, CA 702, MO 539, NY 62), with separations from late May to early June.
WARN notices document at least 2,578 Oracle job cuts in the U.S. in 2026. This counts U.S. filings only, not global cuts.
Oracle had about 141,000 full-time workers as of May 31, 2026, down from about 162,000 a year earlier. It recorded about $1.8B in restructuring costs in fiscal 2026.
Oracle reportedly began another round of layoffs on September 14, 2026 and has not disclosed how many employees were affected. Reports of a further 7,000–10,000 cuts are unconfirmed.

Oracle said the layoffs are expected to be permanent and that the Seattle locations are not closing.
at least 2,578 Oracle job cuts in the U.S. so far in 2026

Oracle has not disclosed how many employees have been affected in this latest round.

caveats: Oracle has not issued a press release giving total layoff numbers. The counts come from state WARN filings (U.S. only), SEC filings and press reports.
The 21,000 headcount decline over fiscal 2026 includes attrition and is not a layoff count. Third-party estimates of 20,000–30,000 cuts (attributed to TD Cowen) are unconfirmed by Oracle.
Restructuring cost figures differ by source: about $1.8B recorded in fiscal 2026 (TheStreet), up to $2.1B planned (March filing, as reported) and about $2.8B (INDmoney blog).
No October or November 2026 round beyond the November 13 separations was confirmed in the sources found. Employee forums mention rumors of more cuts.
Primary sources (the WARN databases and Oracle's 10-K/10-Q) could not be opened directly. Several secondary pages returned 403 errors.
